anchors.name: Create another matrix of same size
anchors.phrase: The easiest approach is create another matrix of the same size.

anchors.name: Original matrix unchanged, direct placement
anchors.phrase: We keep the original matrix unchanged and place every value directly into its rotated destination.

anchors.name: Recall mapping (r, c) -> (c, n - 1 - r)
anchors.phrase: We already know the mapping R, C goes to C n minus 1 minus r.

anchors.name: Apply mapping to elements
anchors.phrase: So now we only need to apply it.

anchors.name: Value 1 at (0, 0)
anchors.phrase: Take 1. 1 is at row 0. Column 0.

anchors.name: Value 1 destination (0, 4)
anchors.phrase: Its destination is row 0. Column 4.

anchors.name: Place 1 in result matrix
anchors.phrase: So we place 1 there in the result matrix.

anchors.name: Value 8 at (1, 2)
anchors.phrase: Now take 8. 8 is at row 1. Column 2.

anchors.name: Value 8 destination (2, 3)
anchors.phrase: Its destination is row 2. Column 3.

anchors.name: Place 8 in result matrix
anchors.phrase: So 8 goes there.

anchors.name: Value 13 at (2, 2)
anchors.phrase: Now 13. 13 is at row 2. Column 2.

anchors.name: Value 13 destination still (2, 2)
anchors.phrase: Its destination is still row 2. Column 2.

anchors.name: Center stays where it is
anchors.phrase: So the center stays where it is.

anchors.name: Value 17 at (3, 1)
anchors.phrase: Now 17. 17 is at row 3. Column 1.

anchors.name: Value 17 calc: row 1, col 4 - 3 = 1
anchors.phrase: Its new row becomes 1. Its new column becomes 4 minus 3, which is 1.

anchors.name: Place 17 at (1, 1)
anchors.phrase: So 17 moves to row 1. Column 1.

anchors.name: The whole idea: read, calc, write safely
anchors.phrase: That is the whole idea. Read a value. From the source matrix, calculate its destination and write it safely into the result matrix.

anchors.name: Source Row 0 (1..5) -> Last Column
anchors.phrase: Now let's complete the full pattern. When we process the first source row, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Those values become the last column of the rotated matrix.

anchors.name: Source Row 1 (6..10) -> Column 3
anchors.phrase: The second source row, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 becomes the next column.

anchors.name: Source Row 2 (11..15) -> Column 2
anchors.phrase: The middle source row becomes the middle column.

anchors.name: Source Row 3 (16..20) -> Column 1
anchors.phrase: Then source row, 3, becomes column 1.

anchors.name: Source Row 4 (21..25) -> Column 0
anchors.phrase: And the final source row becomes column 0.

anchors.name: All processed: correct 90 degree rotation
anchors.phrase: Once every source position has been processed, the result matrix is the correct 90 degree clockwise rotation.

anchors.name: Different matrices, never destroy unread value
anchors.phrase: And because the source and destination are different matrices, we never destroy a value before using it. That makes this method very easy to reason about.

anchors.name: One problem: Extra N x N matrix created
anchors.phrase: But there is one problem. We created another complete n by n matrix.

anchors.phrase: Now let's translate this exact idea into code.
